name: Bronzes, Pages and Drumbeats: Africa's Creative Voices
description: Cities of learning, royal bronzes, Nobel writers, Afrobeat and Nollywood: a tour of the arts of Africa from medieval Cairo to the present.

checkpoints.name: Cities, kings and craft
checkpoints.note: Al-Azhar in Cairo, founded around 970, becomes a leading centre of learning, and Timbuktu grows into a trading and scholarly city. The rock-cut churches of Lalibela are carved in the 1200s, the Mali Empire rises and Mansa Musa's pilgrimage carries its fame abroad, Great Zimbabwe's stone walls rise, and the Benin Bronzes and Kente cloth are made.

checkpoints.name: Pan-African currents
checkpoints.note: Pan-Africanism takes shape as a movement in 1900, and the Great Mosque of Djenné is rebuilt in mud brick in 1907. A generation of writers and musicians is growing up: Mahfouz, Achebe, Makeba, Soyinka and Fela Kuti were all born between 1911 and 1938.

checkpoints.name: Independence and new art
checkpoints.note: Achebe's Things Fall Apart appears in 1958, and many African countries win independence around 1960. Black Girl (1966) is an early landmark of African cinema, Touki Bouki follows in 1973, and Fela Kuti builds Afrobeat in Nigeria in the late 1960s, releasing Zombie in 1977 as a sharp attack on soldiers in power.

checkpoints.name: Prizes and Nollywood
checkpoints.note: Wole Soyinka wins the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, the first Black African writer to do so, and Naguib Mahfouz follows in 1988 as the first Arab laureate. Nollywood, Nigeria's fast-moving video film industry, begins in the 1990s and grows into one of the busiest in the world.
